new_statements.rule_in_words: Barombi is described as a two-tone (L, H) Bantu language with derived HL/LH contours and morphotonological H-spreading, H-lowering and plateauing; the chapter's phonology gives no word-stress or accent rule, and the book's index lists no stress/accent pages within the chapter.
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress statement); tonal processes are confined to specific morphosyntactic environments (61.2.7)
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on syllables/TBUs; tone stability under vowel deletion. Silence on stress is inferred from snippet search plus the volume index, not from a full read of pp. 730-744.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Atindogbé 2025) describes Barombi = Lombe = Rombi (A41, baro1252; villages around Kumba, Meme/Ndian, SW Cameroon); the Oxford Guide index has 'Lombe see Barombi (A41)'. Caution on the name 'lombe': in ALCAM usage (followed by Atindogbe 1990) 'lombe' is the LANGUAGE comprising two dialects, bankon (Abo, A42, bank1256, Dibombari/Littoral) and lombe proper (= Barombi); Atindogbe's 1990 mémoire 'Esquisse phonologique du bankon (dialecte lombe)' and his 1996 Köppe grammar describe Bankon (bank1256), not Barombi, and were excluded as statements for baro1252 (saved 1990 scan kept held by the project as a closely related tonal description, >83% lexical similarity).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NOT the target language: describes Bankon (Abo, A42, bank1256) of Dibombari, Moungo (Littoral); 'lombe' in the title is the ALCAM language name whose two dialects are bankon and lombe (= Barombi): p.1 'Le bankon forme avec le lombe, les deux dialectes de la langue lombe. Sur 250 mots, le taux de ressemblance dépasse 83%'. States 'le bankon est une langue à tons' and inventories five tones (B, H, M, HB, BH); the only passage using 'accent' concerns the H-B pattern of English loanwords (soldier, butter, cotton). No word-stress statement.
